title: Acids, Bases and Salts — Class 10 CBSE Science
subject: Science

slides.title: Acids, Bases and Salts
bullets: Class 10 — CBSE Science
Chapter 2
slides.speaker_notes: From kitchen to lab — chemistry of acids, bases and salts.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Tell acids and bases apart with indicators.
Predict and balance acid + metal / carbonate / oxide reactions.
Explain neutralisation and the H⁺/OH⁻ ions.
Use the pH scale.
Identify common salts (NaOH, NaHCO₃, Na₂CO₃, plaster of Paris) and their uses.

slides.title: Acids and Bases — meet them
bullets: Acids: sour, turn blue litmus red. (lemon, vinegar, HCl)
Bases: bitter, soapy, turn red litmus blue. (soap, NaOH)
WARNING: never taste an unknown chemical!
Use INDICATORS instead.
Common indicators: litmus, methyl orange, phenolphthalein, universal.

slides.title: The three reactions of acids
bullets: 1. Acid + Metal → Salt + H₂↑.
Example: Zn + 2 HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂↑.
2. Acid + Metal carbonate → Salt + H₂O + CO₂↑.
Example: 2 HCl + CaCO₃ → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂↑.
3. Acid + Metal oxide → Salt + H₂O. (CuO + 2 HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂O.)

slides.title: The three reactions of bases
bullets: 1. Base + Non-metallic oxide → Salt + H₂O.
Example: 2 NaOH + CO₂ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O.
2. Base + Acid → Salt + H₂O. (Neutralisation.)
Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.
3. Some bases react with metals: Zn + 2 NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂↑.

slides.title: CO₂ test (lime water)
bullets: CO₂ from a reaction is bubbled through lime water.
Lime water Ca(OH)₂ turns MILKY.
CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O.
The white CaCO₃ precipitate is the milky look.
This is the classic lab test for CO₂.

slides.title: What ALL acids share
bullets: In water, every acid releases H⁺ (forms H₃O⁺).
Every alkaline base releases OH⁻.
These ions are why ALL acids share similar properties.
Pure HCl gas does NOT conduct (no ions); HCl(aq) conducts.
Strong acid: ionises COMPLETELY. Weak acid: ionises PARTIALLY.

slides.title: Strong / weak vs concentrated / dilute
bullets: STRONG: about IONISATION (does it split into ions?).
Strong: HCl, H₂SO₄. Weak: acetic, citric.
CONCENTRATED: about AMOUNT (how much per litre?).
These are INDEPENDENT — you can have:
Dilute strong (HCl 0.01 M) or concentrated weak (acetic 17 M).

slides.title: Safety: dilution of concentrated acid
bullets: Always add ACID to WATER — never the reverse!
Why: dilution releases lots of HEAT.
If you add water to acid, the water boils → acid splashes.
Safe order: large beaker of water + acid added slowly.
Wear safety goggles and rubber gloves.

slides.title: The pH scale
bullets: 0 to 14. 7 = NEUTRAL.
Below 7 = acidic (lower number = more acidic).
Above 7 = basic (higher number = more basic).
Each unit = 10× change in [H⁺].
Universal indicator gives the colour at each pH.

slides.title: pH of common substances
bullets: Lemon ≈ 2; vinegar ≈ 3; coffee ≈ 5.
Pure water = 7.
Blood ≈ 7.4; sea water ≈ 8.
Soap ≈ 10; ammonia ≈ 11.
Drain cleaner / NaOH ≈ 14.

slides.title: Why pH matters in everyday life
bullets: Tooth decay starts when mouth pH < 5.5.
Acid rain (pH < 5.5) damages crops + buildings.
Soil — most plants need pH 6-7.5.
Bee sting (acidic) → relief: baking soda.
Wasp sting (alkaline) → relief: vinegar.

slides.title: Salts — products of acid + base
bullets: Salt: AB + CD → AD + CB; product of acid + base.
NaCl from HCl + NaOH (neutral).
NH₄Cl from HCl + NH₃ (acidic).
CH₃COONa from CH₃COOH + NaOH (basic).
pH of salt depends on parent acid + base strengths.

slides.title: Industrial salts from common salt
bullets: Chlor-alkali: 2 NaCl + 2 H₂O → 2 NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂ (electrolysis).
Bleaching powder: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂.
Baking soda: NaHCO₃ — baking, antacid.
Washing soda: Na₂CO₃·10 H₂O — detergents.
Plaster of Paris: CaSO₄·½ H₂O — casts.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 1. Lemon juice — acid or base? pH range?
2. Balance: Mg + 2 HCl → ?
3. Why pour acid into water?
4. What is the colour of CuSO₄·5 H₂O? After heating?
5. Name two uses of bleaching powder.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Phenolphthalein — colour in base?
Q2. pH of a strong acid?
Q3. Acid + Carbonate → ? + ? + ?.
Q4. Sting of a bee — relief with which?
Show your answers on fingers.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Acid: H⁺ in water; turns blue litmus red.
Base: OH⁻; turns red litmus blue.
3 acid reactions: with metals, carbonates, metal oxides.
Strong / weak (ionisation); concentrated / dilute (amount).
pH 0-14; tooth decay below 5.5.
Common salt → NaOH, Cl₂, baking & washing soda, plaster of Paris.
